handoff: No blocking findings. B1–B20 and B29 are traced to tests; unit, integration (labels) and typecheck are green. B21–B28 (triage labelling) and B30 (docs) were checked by reading and are left for the person to confirm. Minor: glab listLabels reads one page of 100; upgrade on the new layout calls the remote while holding the tick lock; B3 GitLab and B12's upgrade case are not run end to end.

findings.title: Triage labelling and the label docs have no automated test
findings.detail:
B21–B28 are an agent's behaviour, written as instructions in packages/cli/assets/skills/norn-triage/SKILL.md §3–4, packages/cli/assets/workflows/triage.yaml and .agents/workflows/triage.yaml. B30 is docs content (docs/concepts.md labels section, README.md, docs/recipes.md, CONTRIBUTING.md). Read and judged correct: one label per set, existing label kept with 'kept as set; triage would say …', 'Labels not set: … norn upgrade creates it', no label created, deleted or removed, GitLab commands given. The spec has no `criteria` frontmatter, so by default these count as verifier `test`. No test can show an agent's judgement, and quick has no QA step, so they are treated as QA, as review#1 did.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: The person confirms B21–B28 on a real triage run and B30 by reading the docs at `ready`. Next time, add `criteria` frontmatter with verifier agent/person for these items.

findings.title: glab listLabels reads only the first page of 100
findings.detail:
`--per-page 100` with no paging. On a GitLab project with more than 100 labels, doctor warns that labels after page 1 are missing (B16), and unused norn:wf:* labels there are never listed (B10). init and upgrade still come out right through the `_exists` path on create.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Page until a short page comes back (or use glab's --all if it is supported). Verify with a scripted glab that returns 100 labels, then 1.

findings.title: upgrade (new layout) makes the label network calls under the tick lock
findings.detail:
`labelsPart` runs inside the tickLock try block, so a tick waits for up to one listing plus N creates, each up to NETWORK_TIMEOUT_MS. The old-layout path calls labelsPart after lock.release().
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Release the tick lock before labelsPart, as the old-layout path does.

findings.title: GitLab init and upgrade-not-logged-in are not exercised end to end
findings.detail:
B3 is covered by the glab adapter unit tests, the remote contract over a scripted glab and labelCreateCommand('glab'), but no `norn init` runs on glab (FakeRemote is gh only; recorded as F3 in review#1). B12's example is `norn upgrade`, but only init is tested. The code path is shared.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional: give FakeRemote a provider and add one glab init test; add an upgrade B12 case.

findings.title: quoted() leaves a leading `=` bare
findings.detail:
zsh's EQUALS option expands a word that starts with `=`. Label names never start that way, so this is theoretical.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Quote a word that starts with `=`.

findings.title: FakeRemote.createLabel's duplicate check ignores case
findings.detail:
planLabels and the providers compare label names without case; the fake compares with case and always throws gh_exists.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Compare lowercased names.

findings.title: Small cleanups
findings.detail:
The comment says labels run 'after every file is in place', but ensureGitignore/ensureGitattributes run later. gh and glab duplicate the row→RemoteLabel mapping. The `_exists`/`_auth`/`_missing` suffix checks repeat in runtime/labels.ts. init strips the 'labels: ' prefix that labelsLines adds. The core test 'B2, B7, B8' builds its expected value with planLabels. The doctor warning wraps `norn upgrade` in backticks, where B16 quotes it plain.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Optional tidy-ups.

notes.text: B21–B28 (triage sets kind/risk/priority labels) and B30 (label docs) have no automated test. The spec has no criteria frontmatter and quick has no QA step. Please confirm them on a real triage run and by reading docs/concepts.md before merging.
